You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Analysis: The source reveals several defects: only two generated units are registered; `Pull` recognizes only warm/beam; card slot names are not trimmed; readout boots before pulling and therefore never refreshes oxbind's chart; and `cardsCovered` incorrectly makes every readout depend on every card currently in cardwell, conflicting with the unknown-card preservation rule. Cast now returned 2, likely because generated sources changed but registration/build logic remained incomplete. The previous output truncated parts of spin.go/play.go and the combined test may still be running.
Plan: First poll for completion, then print spin.go and play.go separately with line numbers plus the generated registration/files after the failed cast. This will provide the complete implementations and expose the exact cast build failure state before patching.

steps.message:
Analysis: Cast fails because `go` is not on the shell PATH; moreover `exec.Command("go", ...)` resolves the executable before its custom environment is applied, so Spin's PATH addition cannot fix that. The source also hardcodes two unit registrations and known seeds, leaves whitespace in parsed slot names, initializes oxbind in the wrong order, and uses an invalid all-cards coverage gate. We need make cast dynamically generate/register every card, rebuild with an actual Go executable, and make readout use only compiled/carried cards while preserving a previous successful JSON on unsupported card IDs.
Plan: Locate the Go toolchain. Then rewrite the small affected modules: make packbay Fill load all generated card units, make Pull reset/fill carried specs, boot oxbind after Pull, trim card slots, remove the global cardwell coverage check, return void only when the lamp code has no card, and avoid replacing output when a card exists but is not carried. Make cast derive deterministic generated package names for all cards (including temporary ghost cards), regenerate reg.go, and invoke the discovered Go binary. Finally format/build, run cast, and test success, absent-code void, and unsupported-card preservation.

Analysis: Cast now succeeds, `/app/bin/lanternix` remains a native ELF, and generation correctly produced four deterministic units with trimmed slot names and a registration file loading all four. The rebuilt binary should now carry all cards present at cast time. Remaining work is behavioral validation, especially arbitrary lamp paths, void output for a code absent from cardwell, and preservation of a successful readout when a new card appears after cast.
Plan: Run readout against every supported sample and validate JSON and statuses.
